questions.q: Per this lesson, what is Task 1 of the practice lab, and which chapter does it map to?
options: Registering the tenant with Microsoft Purview — Chapter 5
Applying a sensitivity label to a semantic model — Chapter 3
Creating a workspace, assigning it to a domain, and confirming workspace roles — Chapter 1
Setting endorsement to Certified — Chapter 4
questions.explain: Task 1 sets up the tenant-level structure from Chapter 1: a workspace, a domain, and an understanding of workspace roles, before anything else is built.

questions.q: In Task 2, what does 'Load to Tables' actually do, per this lesson's instructions?
options: Applies a sensitivity label automatically to the uploaded file
Permanently deletes the original uploaded file
Turns an uploaded raw file in Files into a real, governed Delta table
Registers the workspace with Microsoft Purview
questions.explain: Task 2 has the learner upload a CSV into Files, then use Load to Tables to create a real Delta table from it, same as Chapter 2 covered.

questions.q: What does the lesson say happens if you try to set an item's endorsement to Certified in Task 4?
options: Certified and Promoted are the exact same setting
Certified is always available to any item owner with no restriction
It may not be possible unless certification is enabled and you're an authorized reviewer in the tenant
Certification can only ever be applied by Microsoft support
questions.explain: Task 4 has the learner notice that Certified requires certification being enabled and the person being an authorized reviewer — unlike Promoted, which any owner can set.

questions.q: According to the lesson's self-check, what should you be able to answer about the item you built, without hunting through five different screens?
options: Only the exact timestamp it was created
Its domain and workspace roles, where its data lives, its sensitivity label, its endorsement status, and who can Build against it
Nothing — the self-check is purely rhetorical with no real answers expected
Only its file size on disk
questions.explain: The five self-check questions map directly to the five lab tasks and the five chapters of the course.

questions.q: Which course does the Data Governance career path continue with after this course, per this lesson's outro?
options: Databricks Unity Catalog Governance
Microsoft Fabric Data Governance (this same course repeated)
The career path ends here, with no further course
Power BI Governance
questions.explain: The lesson's closing section names Databricks Unity Catalog Governance as the next course in the Data Governance path.
